question: What fraction of the observed one-b-tag events is estimated to be background?
question_long: In the ATLAS measurement of lepton distributions in ttbar events at 8 TeV, what fraction of the observed one-b-tag events is estimated to be background?
expect: 2,630 / 21,666 = 12.1% (Table 2, p5); consistent with the ~88% purity in the text
rendered:
According to Table 2 on page 5 of the document, the estimated background fractions for the one-b-tag and two-b-tag events are:

For one-b-tag events:
- Wt single top: 2080 ± 210 (17.8% ± 1.9% of the 11,766 one-b-tag events)
- Z(→ ττ → eμ)+jets: 210 ± 40 (1.8% ± 0.3% of the 11,766 one-b-tag events)
- Diboson: 120 ± 30 (1.0% ± 0.2% of the 11,766 one-b-tag events)
- Misidentified leptons: 220 ± 80 (1.9% ± 0.7% of the 11,766 one-b-tag events)

The purity of the one-b-tag sample in t¯t events is about 88%, so the fraction of the observed one-b-tag events that is estimated to be background is approximately 17.8% + 1.8% + 1.0% + 1.9% = 22.5%
